newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania environment body slams pipeline firm.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania environment body slams pipeline firm.

text.p: Tanzania's main environmental watchdog blasted a state and Zambian-owned pipeline authority on Monday for an oil spill which it said endangered lives in the capital.

The National Environment Management Council (NEMC) said pollution from an oil storage tank leak at Tazama Pipelines Ltd plant in April threatened the lives of residents of Dar es Salaam's Kigamboni suburb.
The leak caused air pollution and a subsequent clean-up effort by the company, which dumped oil in a trench on site, polluted surrounding land, NEMC said.

"Kigamboni residents developed illnesses as a result of the (Tazama) oil spill pollution and such illnesses are still evident and persist," the government-backed NEMC said in a series of half-page newspaper advertisements.
"Urgent measures or steps must be taken in order to abate the situation to protect the health and lives of Dar es Salaam residents which continue to be in grave danger," NEMC said.

Tazama, a mainly Zambian company in which Tanzania has an interest, last week admitted responsibility for the April leak but said it had cleaned up most of the spill. Residual sludge was being recovered for disposal in pits, it said.
The company said it had a $6.4 million budget for improving environmental safeguards and blamed a neighbouring oil company for air pollution, though the company was not named.
NEMC, headed by prominent businessman Reginal Mengi, last week ordered three Dar es Salaam businesses to closed for excessive and unlawful environmental pollution.
The government recently backed a crackdown on polluters with NEMC acting under a directive from vice-president Omar Ali Juma.
Parastatal companies and industries have for years taken advantage of Tanzania's ill-defined and poorly enforced environmental safeguards, according to environmentalists.
